assumptions.assumption: Per-expert token runs are padded upward to block_size multiples before expert_ids are emitted.
assumptions.notes: If padding were not exact, routed GEMM tiles could mix experts or skip rows.

assumptions.assumption: Padding sentinel rows use numel and are masked by fused_moe consumers before token loads.
assumptions.notes: If consumers read sentinel rows as real tokens, padded tiles would load invalid activations.

assumptions.assumption: The align kernel's dynamic shared-memory footprint fits the target device/block configuration.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: shared memory varies depending on the GPU architecture being used
assumptions.notes: CUDA exposes per-block/SM shared-memory limits; too many experts would make the launch fail or reduce occupancy.

assumptions.assumption: CUDA warp-scan code assumes WARP_SIZE lanes and a lane id computed by masking with WARP_SIZE-1.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: warpSize ... number of threads in a warp, commonly 32
assumptions.notes: The CUDA path is safe only when the compiled WARP_SIZE matches the hardware warp width used by shuffles.

assumptions.assumption: All lanes named by the full shuffle mask reach the same __shfl_up_sync call.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: All non-exited threads specified in the mask must execute the intrinsic with the same mask value.
assumptions.notes: If control flow diverged around warp_exclusive_scan, CUDA defines the warp intrinsic behavior as invalid/undefined.

assumptions.assumption: Atomic scatter provides unique per-expert slots but not a semantically observed order.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: Atomic functions perform read-modify-write operations on shared data
assumptions.notes: Atomicity is guaranteed; order is not used by consumers, so scheduling-dependent intra-expert order is acceptable.

assumptions.assumption: The HIP align variant must avoid CUDA-32 warp-scan assumptions on AMD wavefront-64 devices.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: AMD devices return 64 for gfx9 and 32 for gfx10 and above
assumptions.notes: The HIP branch uses blockwide Blelloch scan plus __syncthreads; hard-coding 32-lane warp logic would underuse/break wave64.

assumptions.assumption: The single-token fast path is only selected for M == 1 and topk <= 32.
assumptions.notes: The one-warp layout writes one block per top-k slot; larger topk would leave lanes unrepresented.

assumptions.assumption: Single-token router top-k expert IDs are distinct, with a lane tie-break as robustness only.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/align_single_token.cuh:42-43 "ids are distinct ... tie-break on lane keeps this robust"
assumptions.notes: If caller supplied duplicate expert IDs, one-block-per-expert assumptions and expert_ids layout would change.

assumptions.assumption: The small-numel Triton fast path remains profitable because NP<=64 pair tensors stay effectively register/local enough.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_align_small_numel.py:37-40 "pairwise comparisons ... measured slower than the two-kernel path"
assumptions.notes: This is measurement-backed, not a public ISA/compiler guarantee; register allocation changes could erase the win.

assumptions.assumption: Fused shared experts are represented by reducing routed topk and appending shared-expert IDs after routed experts.
assumptions.notes: Downstream kernels must interpret appended IDs >= num_experts as shared experts, not normal routed experts.

assumptions.assumption: topk must be greater than num_fused_shared_experts before the fused gate runs.
assumptions.notes: Without at least one routed slot, routed_sum/renormalization and selected expert writes would be ill-defined.

assumptions.assumption: When bias is present, selection uses biased scores but output weights use original score values.
assumptions.notes: Violating this model-specific contract changes router weights, not just which experts are selected.

assumptions.assumption: AOT top-k softmax templates require THREADS_PER_ROW to divide the CUDA warp width.
assumptions.spec_excerpt: warpSize ... number of threads in a warp, commonly 32
assumptions.notes: The code statically checks this compile-time partition; a mismatch would break row-to-warp reductions.

assumptions.assumption: routed_scaling_factor is a scalar per MoE invocation and can be applied once per combined output element.
assumptions.notes: A per-token or per-expert scale would not be equivalent to a single post-sum multiply.

assumptions.assumption: Scale fusion in moe_sum_reduce happens after accumulation, matching a separate post-reduction multiply order.
assumptions.notes: Moving scale inside the top-k loop could change rounding; current placement preserves post-sum semantics.

assumptions.assumption: Gate-output scaling is explicit and guarded by apply_routed_scaling_factor_on_output.
assumptions.notes: The flag prevents accidental double-scaling when scale is instead fused in the combine/reduce path.

assumptions.assumption: Inputs to CUDA moe_sum_reduce are contiguous [token, topk, hidden] tensors with matching output shape.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/moe/moe_sum_reduce.cu:230-236 "3D tensor ... expect input to be contiguous"
assumptions.notes: Stride arithmetic assumes this layout; non-contiguous tensors would sum wrong rows or hidden positions.

assumptions.assumption: The bf16 vector path is selected only when hidden_dim is divisible by 8 and token_num is large enough.
assumptions.notes: The vectorized load/store packs eight bf16 values; unsupported tails fall back to scalar kernels.

assumptions.assumption: uint4 vector loads/stores require 16-byte alignment that the framework allocation/layout must supply.
assumptions.notes: CUDA specifies uint4 alignment; code checks divisibility/contiguity but relies on tensor storage alignment.

assumptions.assumption: The JIT topk_sum vector path requires hidden dimension K divisible by 8.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/moe/topk_sum.cuh:87 "K must be divisible by 8 for vectorized loads"
assumptions.notes: If violated, the JIT refuses the specialization rather than issuing partial vector loads.

assumptions.assumption: Triton fused_moe consumes sorted_token_ids/expert_ids only up to num_tokens_post_padded.
assumptions.notes: The align contract is safe only if padded buffer tail beyond the published count is not consumed.

assumptions.assumption: Grouped program-ID ordering is expected to improve L2 locality for expert GEMM tiles.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:168 "grouped ordering to promote L2 data reuse"
assumptions.spec_excerpt: block-structured iteration spaces ... optimize programs for data locality
assumptions.notes: The performance claim depends on compiler/GPU cache behavior; incorrect ordering would not change semantics.

assumptions.assumption: SwiGLU activation fusion is valid only under wrapper-checked dtype/layout/hook constraints.
assumptions.code_evidence: 89e1316e:python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:124 "fuse_swiglu_interleaved set on an incompatible fused_moe call"
assumptions.notes: If fused when bias/hooks/quant/layout differ, it would combine the wrong gate/up projection semantics.

assumptions.assumption: Stable sorting flattened topk_ids creates contiguous expert segments and preserves pair order within equal expert IDs.
assumptions.notes: seg_indptr/searchsorted assumes equal expert IDs occupy one interval; instability would affect reproducible src2dst order.

assumptions.assumption: Filtered -1 expert IDs are shifted out before DeepEP segment pointers and src2dst destinations are used.
assumptions.notes: Without consistent -1 removal, local expert segment offsets would be negative or off by the filtered count.

assumptions.assumption: Post-reorder accumulation applies top-k weights and routed scaling exactly once while mapping src2dst rows back to tokens.
assumptions.notes: A mismatch would double-scale, omit weights, or accumulate a routed pair into the wrong token output.

assumptions.assumption: DeepEP dispatcher outputs expose the exact hidden_states/topk_ids/topk_weights metadata layout consumed by EP runners.
assumptions.notes: The fused EP runners rely on this tuple layout; external DeepEP changes would require adapter updates.
